mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months indicates monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in FEDFUNDS decline periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month upward trend in housing starts (HOUST) reflects strengthening consumer demand and construction activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in HOUST rise periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC remains negative in any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the prior 3 months signals improving labor market conditions that increase corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in UNRATE decline periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0% for three consecutive months, restrictive monetary policy increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in FEDFUNDS > 4.0% periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC is positive in any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE rises above 6.5% for two consecutive months, deteriorating labor market conditions reduce consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in UNRATE > 6.5% periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC is above -0.03 in any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in PAYEMS and HOUST over the prior 3 months indicate robust labor market and consumer demand expansion, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through joint economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both increase > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in PAYEMS/HOUST rise periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for interaction falls below 0.03 in any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% annualized), a decline in real sales (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.5% annualized and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in CPIAUCSL > 3.5% and RSAFS decline periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for interaction is above -0.03 in any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During recessionary periods (GDPC1 growth < 0% for 2 quarters), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 indicates worsening economic output, generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 0% for 2 quarters and INDPRO < 95.0
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in GDPC1 < 0% and INDPRO < 95.0 periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for interaction falls below -0.03 in any 3-year window.
